usdRate.note: The US dollar is the reference currency: 1 by definition.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index news release, September 2026
inflation_cpi.note: CPI-U rose 3.7% in the 12 months to September 2026 (not seasonally adjusted); released 14 October 2026. World Bank 2024 average 2.9%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Federal Reserve 2% longer-run goal for PCE inflation; CPI-U 3.7% (Sep 2026, BLS)
inflation_projection.note: The Fed's 2% goal is for PCE prices, which run a few tenths below CPI, and inflation has stayed above goal since 2021, so 2.7% CPI inflation is used.

policy_rate.sourceName: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, open market operations: federal funds target range
policy_rate.note: Target range 3.75-4.00% (upper bound shown) after a 25 basis point rise on 17 September 2026; the range was unchanged through 31 October 2026 (FRED DFEDTARU).

savings_account_rate.sourceName: FDIC, National Rates and Rate Caps, October 2026: savings
savings_account_rate.note: National average savings rate 0.38% (money market 0.63%, interest checking 0.07%); online high-yield savings accounts pay much more. Interest is taxable.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: FDIC, National Rates and Rate Caps, October 2026: 3-month CD
fdr_3m_rate.note: National average 3-month certificate of deposit rate 1.14% (6-month 1.39%).

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: FDIC, National Rates and Rate Caps, October 2026: 12-month CD
fdr_1y_rate.note: National average 12-month CD rate 1.76% (24-month 1.55%, 60-month 1.41%). Many banks pay far more than the deposit-weighted average; 1-year Treasury yield was 4.36% on 30 Oct 2026.

dps_rate.note: US banks do not commonly sell monthly recurring-deposit products and the FDIC national rates cover only savings, checking, money market and CDs; no published rate was found.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No weighted average deposit rate across banks is published by the Federal Reserve or FDIC in this form; World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no US series. FDIC national averages (October 2026): savings 0.38%, 12-month CD 1.76%.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.sourceName: U.S. Treasury (TreasuryDirect), Series I savings bonds: interest rates
sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Composite rate 4.26% for I bonds issued May-October 2026 (fixed 0.90% plus inflation 1.67% a half-year); bonds issued November 2026-April 2027 earn 5.51% (fixed 1.40%). Rate resets every 6 months with CPI; cashing in before 5 years forfeits the last 3 months' interest; USD 10,000 a year limit per person electronically.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, daily Treasury par yield curve rates: 3-month

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, daily Treasury par yield curve rates: 5-year

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: U.S. Department of the Treasury, daily Treasury par yield curve rates: 10-year

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Internal Revenue Service, tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
tax_bank_interest.note: No withholding on interest for residents; interest is ordinary income. 22% is the federal marginal rate for a single filer with taxable income USD 50,401-105,700 in 2026 (12% below that); most states add their own income tax (eight have none). Interest in IRAs and 401(k)s is tax-deferred or tax-free (Roth).

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: TreasuryDirect, I bonds; IRS 2026 federal brackets
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: I bond interest is subject to federal income tax at the marginal rate (22% for a middle earner) but exempt from state and local tax; tax can be deferred until the bond is cashed and may be excluded if used for qualified higher education. Treasury bill and bond interest is also state-tax-free.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), deposit insurance
deposit_insurance_limit.note: At least USD 250,000 per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, per ownership category. Credit unions are insured to the same limit by the NCUA.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit: commercial bank interest rate on credit card plans, all accounts
credit_card_rate_cap.note: 21.19% APR on all accounts in August 2026 (22.36% on accounts assessed interest), released 7 October 2026. There is no general federal cap on credit card interest.

equity_return_low.sourceName: S&P 500 7,580 on 30 Oct 2026, +10.8% in a year, near its October 2026 record (Trading Economics)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: from high valuations US shares deliver well below their 10-year record, only a little above Treasuries.

equity_return_base.sourceName: S&P 500 (Trading Economics); after-tax safe rate about 3.2% (3-month bill 4.16% less 22% federal tax, US Treasury)
equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 3.5-4 points above the after-tax Treasury bill rate, below the S&P 500's strong 10-year record because valuations are high.

equity_return_high.note: High case: US shares continue close to their long-run total return of about 9-10% a year with dividends.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026, 31% below the January 2026 high (Trading Economics)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold drifts after the 2025-26 spike and lags inflation.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); Fed 2% goal
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with inflation plus a little over the long run.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of part of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in dollars.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: 3-month Treasury bill 4.16%, 12-month CD 1.76% national average (US Treasury; FDIC)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: short rates fall back towards 3% and are taxed at about 22%, or savings sit in low-rate bank accounts.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 3-month bill 4.16% and 1-year Treasury 4.36% less 22% federal tax = 3.2-3.4% (US Treasury)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: Treasury bills, notes and competitive CDs after 22% federal tax, assuming rates ease a little.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: 5-year Treasury 4.71% (US Treasury); I bonds 5.51% from November 2026 (TreasuryDirect)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: locking in today's 5-year Treasury or I bond rates, partly inside tax-advantaged accounts.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: Neither the NAIC nor state insurance departments publish an industry-wide life insurance claim settlement ratio; no official figure was found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life insurance is widely sold in the US, but no regulator or government body publishes indicative premiums per USD 1,000 of cover by age; insurer and broker quote tools were not used.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Indicative only: USD 10,600 is the 2026 legal maximum an individual on a Marketplace (ACA-compliant) plan pays out of pocket in a year for in-network care (USD 21,200 for a family); one major hospital stay with surgery often reaches the plan's deductible or this limit. Uninsured patients face the full bill.

health_premium_table.note: US health insurance is priced per plan (by age, location, metal tier and tobacco use), not per sum insured; no official premium table per USD 100,000 of cover exists.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: BLS CPI September 2026: medical care +1.5%, medical care services +2.5% over 12 months
goal_inflation_health.note: Measured medical CPI is low this year, but US health costs and premiums have long risen faster than general prices, so 4% is used.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: BLS CPI September 2026: education index +3.8% over 12 months
goal_inflation_education.note: Education prices are rising faster than general inflation, and college costs have a long record of doing so, so 4% is used.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 77.4, women 82.2 (UN WPP estimate for 2026). World Bank 2024: 78.9 (men 76.5, women 81.4).

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 28.5 (2025, World Bank), 35.5 (2040) and 41.6 (2065, populationpyramid.net/united-states-of-america/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Social Security Act section 216(l), 42 U.S.C. 416(l) (Cornell LII)
retirement_age_default.note: Full retirement age is 67 for anyone reaching 62 after 2021 (born 1960 or later), men and women alike; reduced benefits from 62, delayed credits to 70. There is no mandatory retirement age for most private employees.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: U.S. Office of Personnel Management, FERS retirement eligibility
retirement_age_government.note: Federal employees under FERS can retire on an immediate unreduced annuity at 62 with 5 years' service, 60 with 20 years, or the minimum retirement age (57 for those born 1970 or later) with 30 years; there is no mandatory retirement age for most federal jobs.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: 3-month Treasury bill 4.16% (US Treasury); FDIC national CD averages
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: short rates fall back and savings earn less after tax.

retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 3-month Treasury bill rate for a middle-income retiree.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a retiree ladders Treasuries, I bonds and competitive CDs at about today's rates.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: After-tax safe rate about 3.2%; S&P 500 valuations (Trading Economics)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag, held mostly in 401(k)s and IRAs.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 7% and half bonds and bills at about 3%, in tax-advantaged accounts.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix in tax-advantaged accounts.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: Social Security Administration, Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026 (Federal Register)
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Supplemental Security Income (SSI) federal payment standard USD 994 a month for an individual (USD 1,491 for a couple) in 2026; many states add a supplement. Paid to people 65+ (or disabled) with very low income and resources.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: 42 U.S.C. 1382c(a)(1)(A), definition of aged individual for SSI (Cornell LII)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: SSI is paid from 65 regardless of work history, but is means-tested on income and resources (countable resources up to USD 2,000 for an individual, USD 3,000 for a couple) and requires US citizenship or qualifying immigration status.

gratuity_rule.note: US federal law (Fair Labor Standards Act) requires no severance or end-of-service payment; any severance or retirement payment is at the employer's discretion or set by contract (U.S. Department of Labor, severance pay: https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/wages/severancepay).

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Social Security Administration, Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026 (Federal Register); 42 U.S.C. 416(l)
public_pension_scheme.note: Social Security (Old-Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance): earnings-related, funded by payroll tax (6.2% employee plus 6.2% employer) on earnings up to USD 184,500 in 2026; 40 quarters of coverage (about 10 years) needed. Full benefit at 67 for those born 1960 or later, reduced from 62, larger to 70. Benefits rose 2.8% in January 2026 under the automatic CPI-W cost-of-living adjustment; up to 85% of benefits can be federally taxable.

savings_account.note: National average rates are low; online high-yield savings and money market accounts pay close to Treasury bill rates. FDIC-insured to USD 250,000.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring-deposit product; savers use automatic transfers into savings accounts or brokerage and retirement accounts.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: Bought from the Treasury at TreasuryDirect, up to USD 10,000 a year per person; Series EE bonds are also sold (doubling guaranteed in 20 years).

tbill_91d.note: Individuals can buy at auction through TreasuryDirect or a broker; interest is exempt from state and local tax.

equity_fund.note: Usually held in a 401(k), IRA or Roth IRA for tax advantages.

gold.note: Legal to buy; the U.S. Mint issues gold bullion coins. Gains on physical gold are taxed as collectibles (up to 28% federal).

centralBank.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

insuranceRegulator.name: State insurance departments (coordinated through the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, NAIC)
insuranceRegulator.note: Insurance is regulated by each state; the NAIC is the states' standard-setting body.

insuranceComplaints.name: Your state insurance department (NAIC directory)
insuranceComplaints.note: Find your state insurance department and file a complaint there.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
oldAgeAllowance.note: Means-tested monthly payment for people 65+ or disabled with little income and resources.

publicHealthCover.name: Medicare (65+), Medicaid and the Health Insurance Marketplace
publicHealthCover.note: Medicare covers people 65+; Medicaid covers low-income people; others buy cover through employers or HealthCare.gov (https://www.healthcare.gov/).

depositInsurance.name: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC)
depositInsurance.note: Credit union deposits are insured by the NCUA.

statistics.name: U.S. Census Bureau
statistics.note: Consumer prices are published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/).
